newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec threatens to order public sector wage cut.
newsitem.headline: Quebec threatens to order public sector wage cut.

text.p: Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard threatened on Thursday to introduce a special law imposing a six percent wage reduction on public sector employees who do not accept government ordered job cuts.

Bouchard told Quebec's National Assembly that law could be introduced in a special session on Friday. The Premier made the announcement as unions representing 440,000 public sector employees continued to negotiate with government officials.
The Quebec government is seeking to eliminate 15,000 public sector jobs by July 1 as part of its efforts to reduce its budget deficit to C$2.2 billion in 1997/98.

Although the Quebec government reached a tentative agreement with unions representing about 100,000 health care workers late Wednesday night, talks continued with union leaders for 250,000 other workers.

Some union leaders said on Thursday that they were approaching an agreement with the government, but others, notably the head of Quebec's largest teachers union, said they would request a personal meeting with Bouchard to resolve the impasse.
